# Creating an Amazon S3 direct-query data source for OpenSearch Service

You can create a new Amazon S3 direct-query data source for OpenSearch Service through the AWS Management Console or the API. Each new data source uses the AWS Glue Data Catalog to manage tables that represent Amazon S3 buckets.

## Prerequisites

Before you can create a data source, you must have an OpenSearch domain running version 2.13 or later. You must also have one or more S3 buckets, including the buckets that contain the data you want to query and a bucket in which to store query checkpoints.

One or more AWS Glue tables are optional as a prerequisite. However, querying data on Amazon S3 requires tables set up in the AWS Glue Data Catalog that point to the S3 data. You must create these Glue tables using OpenSearch Query Workbench, because existing Hive tables are not compatible. If this is the first time you are setting up an Amazon S3 data source, you must create an admin data source to configure all of your AWS Glue Data Catalog tables. After you create your tables, you can create new Amazon S3 data sources and restrict access to limited tables.

A manually created IAM role is also optional and can be used to manage access to your data source. Alternatively, OpenSearch Service can create a role automatically with the required permissions. If you choose a manually created IAM role, you must ensure it has all necessary permissions by attaching the required policies from the IAM console. In the console, you can choose **Create a new role** to automatically create a role for the data source. If tables have not been created yet, you should provide access to the default database.

## Creating the data source

The AddDataSource API operation creates a new data source in your domain. After you create a data source, OpenSearch Service provides an OpenSearch Dashboards link. You use this link to configure access control, define tables, install out-of-the-box integrations, and query your data.

## Access control

If you enabled fine-grained access control after creating a data source, you must map non-admin users to an IAM role with AWS Glue Data Catalog access in order to run direct queries. Be aware that a user with read access to the request index for a given data source can read all queries against that data source, and a user with read access to the result index can read results for all queries against that data source. The glue_access backend role is mapped to the ARN of the AWS Glue role that needs permission to call your domain.

## Permissions for a manually created role

A manually created role's permissions must allow access to the specific data source and allow OpenSearch Service to assume the role. Broader permissions such as s3:* or the AdministratorAccess policy encompass the least-privilege permissions in the sample policy. To support Amazon S3 buckets in different accounts, you need to include a condition in the Amazon S3 policy and add the appropriate account. The role must also have a trust policy allowing the service directquery.opensearchservice.amazonaws.com to perform sts:AssumeRole.

## Automatically created fine-grained access control role

If fine-grained access control is enabled in OpenSearch Service, a new fine-grained access control role named AWSOpenSearchDirectQuery<name of data source> is automatically created for the data source. By default, this role has access to direct query data source indexes only. It is recommended not to adjust its access. If you delete the data source, the automatically created fine-grained access control role is deleted as well, and deleting the role removes access for any other users mapped to it.

# Creating an Amazon S3 direct-query data source for OpenSearch Service

## Before you begin

- **IAM permissions policy for the manually created role.** If you choose to manage access with a manually created IAM role, you need a permissions policy that grants S3, AWS Glue, and OpenSearch access. The least-privilege sample policy and the steps for attaching it are described in the "Manually created IAM role" section later on this page. Attach the policy to the role from the IAM console before you create the data source.

## Overview

You can create a new Amazon S3 direct-query data source for OpenSearch Service through the AWS Management Console or the API. Each new data source uses the AWS Glue Data Catalog to manage tables that represent Amazon S3 buckets.

## Requirements

Creating a data source holds only when both of the following are in place. You must have an OpenSearch domain with version 2.13 or later, and you must have one or more S3 buckets. These buckets include the ones containing the data you want to query and a bucket to store query checkpoints in.

One or more AWS Glue tables are optional as a prerequisite. However, querying data on Amazon S3 requires that you have tables set up in the AWS Glue Data Catalog to point to the S3 data. You must create the Glue tables using OpenSearch Query Workbench. Existing Hive tables are not compatible.

If this is the first time you are setting up an Amazon S3 data source, you must create an admin data source to configure all of your AWS Glue Data Catalog tables. After you create your tables, you can create new Amazon S3 data sources and restrict access to limited tables.

A manually created IAM role is optional and can be used to manage access to your data source. Alternatively, OpenSearch Service can create a role automatically with the required permissions.

## Creating the data source

In the console, you can choose **Create a new role** to automatically create a role for the data source. If tables have not been created yet, you should provide access to the default database. If you choose a manually created IAM role instead, you must ensure it has all necessary permissions by attaching the required policies from the IAM console.

Through the API, the AddDataSource operation creates a new data source in your domain.

You must create the data source before the next step. After you create it, OpenSearch Service provides an OpenSearch Dashboards link that you use to configure access control, define tables, install out-of-the-box integrations, and query your data.

## Manually created IAM role

A manually created role's permissions must allow access to the specific data source and allow OpenSearch Service to assume the role. Broader permissions such as `s3:*` or the AdministratorAccess policy encompass the least-privilege permissions in the sample policy. To support Amazon S3 buckets in different accounts, you need to include a condition in the Amazon S3 policy and add the appropriate account.

The role must also have a trust policy allowing the service `directquery.opensearchservice.amazonaws.com` to perform `sts:AssumeRole`.

## Access control

If you enabled fine-grained access control after creating a data source, you must map non-admin users to an IAM role with AWS Glue Data Catalog access in order to run direct queries. The `glue_access` backend role is mapped to the ARN of the AWS Glue role that needs permission to call your domain.

Be aware of the following read permissions. A user with read access to the request index for a given data source can read all queries against that data source. A user with read access to the result index can read results for all queries against that data source.

## Automatically created fine-grained access control role

If fine-grained access control is enabled in OpenSearch Service, a new fine-grained access control role named `AWSOpenSearchDirectQuery<name of data source>` is automatically created for the data source. By default, this role has access to direct query data source indexes only. It is recommended not to adjust the access of the automatically created role.

If you delete the data source, the automatically created fine-grained access control role is deleted. Deleting the role removes access for any other users mapped to it.

# Creating an Amazon S3 Direct-Query Data Source for OpenSearch Service

You can create a new Amazon S3 direct-query data source for OpenSearch Service through the AWS Management Console or the API. Each new data source uses the AWS Glue Data Catalog to manage tables that represent Amazon S3 buckets. The AddDataSource API operation creates a new data source in your domain.

## Prerequisites

Before you can create a data source, you must have an OpenSearch domain with version 2.13 or later. You must also have one or more S3 buckets, including the buckets containing the data you want to query and a bucket in which to store query checkpoints.

One or more AWS Glue tables are optional as a prerequisite. However, querying data on Amazon S3 requires tables set up in the AWS Glue Data Catalog that point to the S3 data. You must create these Glue tables using OpenSearch Query Workbench, and existing Hive tables are not compatible. If this is the first time you are setting up an Amazon S3 data source, you must create an admin data source to configure all of your AWS Glue Data Catalog tables. After you create your tables, you can create new Amazon S3 data sources and restrict access to limited tables.

A manually created IAM role is also optional and can be used to manage access to your data source. Alternatively, OpenSearch Service can create a role automatically with the required permissions. In the console, you can choose **Create a new role** to automatically create a role for the data source. If tables have not been created yet, you should provide access to the default database. If you choose a manually created IAM role, you must ensure it has all necessary permissions by attaching the required policies from the IAM console.

## Manually Created Role Requirements

A manually created role's permissions must allow access to the specific data source and allow OpenSearch Service to assume the role. Broader permissions, such as s3:* or the AdministratorAccess policy, encompass the least-privilege permissions in the sample policy. To support Amazon S3 buckets in different accounts, you need to include a condition in the Amazon S3 policy and add the appropriate account. The role must also have a trust policy allowing the service directquery.opensearchservice.amazonaws.com to perform sts:AssumeRole.

## After Creating a Data Source

After you create a data source, OpenSearch Service provides an OpenSearch Dashboards link. You use this link to configure access control, define tables, install out-of-the-box integrations, and query your data.

If you enabled fine-grained access control after creating a data source, you must map non-admin users to an IAM role with AWS Glue Data Catalog access in order to run direct queries. The glue_access backend role is mapped to the ARN of the AWS Glue role that needs permission to call your domain.

Be aware of the following access considerations. A user with read access to the request index for a given data source can read all queries against that data source. Similarly, a user with read access to the result index can read results for all queries against that data source.

## Automatically Created Fine-Grained Access Control Role

If fine-grained access control is enabled in OpenSearch Service, a new fine-grained access control role named AWSOpenSearchDirectQuery<name of data source> is automatically created for the data source. By default, this role has access to direct query data source indexes only. It is recommended not to adjust the access of this automatically created role.

If you delete the data source, the automatically created fine-grained access control role is deleted. Deleting this role removes access for any other users mapped to it.

# Creating an Amazon S3 direct-query data source for OpenSearch Service

## Before you begin

Complete the following prerequisites before you create a data source. Each one is needed before the step that uses it.

- **An OpenSearch Service domain running version 2.13 or later.** Steps: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/opensearch-service/latest/developerguide/createupdatedomains.html
- **One or more S3 buckets containing the data you want to query.** Steps: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/create-bucket-overview.html
- **An S3 bucket to store query checkpoints.** Steps: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/create-bucket-overview.html
- **AWS Glue Data Catalog tables pointing to the S3 data (optional).** Create them using OpenSearch Query Workbench. If the tables have not been created yet, you can provide access to the default database initially.
- **A manually created IAM role with a required permissions policy and trust policy (optional).** You need this only if you do not let OpenSearch Service create the role automatically. Steps: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_create_for-custom.html
- **An identity-based permissions policy (es, glue, and s3 actions) attached to the manually created role.** Steps are on this page.
- **A trust policy on the manually created role that allows OpenSearch Service to assume it.** Steps are on this page.

## Overview

You can create a new Amazon S3 direct-query data source for OpenSearch Service through the AWS Management Console or the API. This works only when both of the following hold: you have an OpenSearch domain with version 2.13 or later, and you have one or more S3 buckets, including the buckets containing the data you want to query and a bucket to store query checkpoints in. Each new data source uses the AWS Glue Data Catalog to manage tables that represent Amazon S3 buckets.

## AWS Glue tables

One or more AWS Glue tables are optional as a prerequisite. However, querying data on Amazon S3 requires that you have tables set up in the AWS Glue Data Catalog to point to the S3 data. You must create the Glue tables using OpenSearch Query Workbench. Existing Hive tables are not compatible.

If this is the first time you are setting up an Amazon S3 data source, you must create an admin data source to configure all of your AWS Glue Data Catalog tables. After you create your tables, you can create new Amazon S3 data sources and restrict access to limited tables. If tables have not been created yet, you should provide access to the default database.

## IAM role

A manually created IAM role is optional and can be used to manage access to your data source. Alternatively, OpenSearch Service can create a role automatically with the required permissions. In the console, you can choose **Create a new role** to automatically create a role for the data source.

If you choose a manually created IAM role, you must ensure it has all necessary permissions by attaching the required policies from the IAM console. The role's permissions must allow access to the specific data source and allow OpenSearch Service to assume the role. Broader permissions such as `s3:*` or the `AdministratorAccess` policy encompass the least-privilege permissions in the sample policy. To support Amazon S3 buckets in different accounts, you need to include a condition in the Amazon S3 policy and add the appropriate account. The role must also have a trust policy allowing the service `directquery.opensearchservice.amazonaws.com` to perform `sts:AssumeRole`.

## Create the data source

The `AddDataSource` API operation creates a new data source in your domain. You can also create the data source in the console, as described above.

## After you create the data source

Creating the data source must happen before the next steps, because after you create a data source, OpenSearch Service provides an OpenSearch Dashboards link. You use this link to configure access control, define tables, install out-of-the-box integrations, and query your data.

## Access control

If you enabled fine-grained access control after creating a data source, you must map non-admin users to an IAM role with AWS Glue Data Catalog access in order to run direct queries. Keep in mind that a user with read access to the request index for a given data source can read all queries against that data source. A user with read access to the result index can read results for all queries against that data source. The `glue_access` backend role is mapped to the ARN of the AWS Glue role that needs permission to call your domain.

If fine-grained access control is enabled in OpenSearch Service, a new fine-grained access control role named `AWSOpenSearchDirectQuery<name of data source>` is automatically created for the data source. By default, this role has access to direct query data source indexes only. It is recommended not to adjust the access of the automatically created role. If you delete the data source, the automatically created role is deleted, and deleting it removes access for any other users mapped to the role.
